To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we generated a transgenic mouse model of the hereditary hemorrage telangiectasia by using an ICAM-2-promoter driven endoglin transgene, that we developed a vascular gene therapy approach to treat this disease by using an adenovirus driven by the endoglin or ICAM-2 promoter, and that this approach is applicable to other vascular diseases.
we have generated transgenic mice that express endoglin specifically in the vascular endothelum and have used these promoters to drive vascular expression of human endoglin.
the endoglin and the ICAM-2 promoter can be used to drive gene transfer to the endothelum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
gene transfer to the vasculatory system and the development of novel gene transfer vectors for the treatment of vascular disorders, including hereditary hemorrhagic disorders.
the development of new gene transfer systems that allow the selective expression of therapeutic genes in the vascular system.
the development of new strategies for vascular gene transfer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vascular gene transfer driven by endothelial-specific promoters can be used in vivo for the treatment of a variety of vascular disorders.
vascular gene therapy has been shown to be a feasible approach for the treatment of vascular diseases.
the endoglin and/or ICAM-2 promoter driven gene therapy is a feasible and promising approach for treatment of the heriditary hemorrhagic telangiecta type 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed two novel gene transfer systems that target the endothelium.
vascular gene delivery can be achieved using endoglin and/or ICAM-2 as promoters.
we have shown for the first time that the vascular endothelum can be genetically targeted using endoglin and/or ICAM-2 promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endoglin and the ICAM-2 gene promoters can be used for vascular gene transfer.
we have developed a new approach for gene therapy in the vasculature by using the endoglin promoter to target gene expression specifically to the vascular endothelum.
we have developed two novel gene transfer vectors that can be used to target the vasculature in vivo, and that can be used for the treatment of a number of vascular diseases.
